welcome: What AuditISA does, how every engagement file is organised, and what to do while the screen is working. Who: everyone in the firm. What AuditISA does AuditISA holds your firm's engagement files. Each engagement (one client, one financial year) has its own engagement file, built on the International Standards on Auditing (ISA) and on the OHADA rules. The engagement file lists every task of the audit, from accepting the client to archiving the engagement file. You prepare each task, a more senior colleague reviews it, and the partner signs, depending on your firm's sign-off policy. Only the people on an engagement's team can open that engagement: your role in the firm alone does not give you access to an engagement. How an engagement file is organised Every engagement file follows the same four phases, in the order of the audit. The engagement's dashboard shows one ring per phase, with the percentage done, and the groups of tasks beside it. Phase (top bar) On the dashboard Task groups Planning Planning and Risk Identification P1 to P7: acceptance and continuance, independence and team, understanding the business, entity-level controls and IT, fraud risks, materiality, planning review and approval Strategy and risks Strategy and Risk Assessment S1 to S6: transactions and walkthroughs, controls and IT, combined risk assessment, specific risk areas, audit procedure design, audit strategy memorandum Execution Execution E1 to E6: tests of controls, control updates, substantive procedures, specific procedures, registers and opening balances Conclusion Conclusion and Reporting C1 to C6: audit differences, final review, representations, review and approval, statutory reports and communications, documentation and archiving Each task has a code (for example P6.1) that stays the same on every engagement file, so the whole team speaks the same language. Click a group to see its Task list with each task's status and due date. Some working papers are Conditional papers: they only come onto the engagement file, and into the percentage, when an answer elsewhere calls for them. The engagement dashboard also shows My tasks (what is open and assigned to you), Review notes and findings (Notes for me, Notes by me, Deficiencies, Misstatements) and a Calendar of the next deadlines, with the overdue ones counted. If some tasks have nobody to prepare them, a warning says so, with Assign them. If the dashboard says Profile not finished: finish it to get your tasks, the engagement profile still needs answers. Click Finish the profile: the profile decides which tasks the engagement file needs. The engagement dashboard: one ring per phase When the screen is working When AuditISA needs a moment to fetch or save something, a thin moving bar appears along the very top of the screen. Wait until it disappears before you click again. Quick actions do not show the bar at all. See also: The top bar, Signing in for the first time, The engagement dashboard
top-bar: The bar at the top of the screen stays in place on every page and takes you anywhere in AuditISA. Who: everyone in the firm. What each item does From left to right, the top bar holds: Item What it does The A logo and your firm's name Takes you back to your home page (Dashboard) from anywhere. Dashboard and Engagements Shown when you are not inside an engagement. Engagements lists all the engagements you are a team member of. Planning, Strategy and risks, Execution, Conclusion, Tasks Shown when you are inside an engagement. Each phase name opens that part of the engagement's dashboard. Tasks lists every task of the engagement file. ENGAGEMENTS switcher Shows the engagement you are in (or Select engagement). Click it to see your Recent engagements and jump to another one, or click All engagements. Search… Type at least two letters. Results come in four groups: Engagements, Tasks, In the methodology (the guidance text) and In the answers (what the team has written). Engagement tools (four squares) Shown inside an engagement. Opens the engagement's tools, such as the trial balance, the analytics and the lists of findings. Timesheet (clock) Shown outside an engagement. Opens your timesheet (see Recording your time). Apps (nine dots) Lists the parts of AuditISA you may open: Audit (engagements and engagement files), Timesheet, and, for the firm administrator, Users and Settings. Help (?) Opens this user manual at the page about the screen you are on (Help on this page). Search the manual or browse its contents from there. Notifications (bell) A red figure shows how many messages you have not read. Click a message to go straight to the task, engagement or invitation it is about. See all notifications opens the full list. Settings (cog) A short menu. Inside an engagement it starts with Engagement record, Log time on this engagement and Budget and actual. It always holds Clients, My invitations and Preferences. Partners also see the firm's sign-off rules and file index; the firm administrator also sees the audit log, Users and Settings. EN / FR Switches the whole tool between English and French. The page reloads in the language you chose, and AuditISA remembers it next time. Your name, role and initials Shows who is signed in and your role in the firm (for example Manager or Quality reviewer). Sign out Ends your session. Always sign out on a shared computer. The top bar, inside an engagement On a phone, the bar takes several lines: your firm, Help, the bell, the cog and Sign out first, then the switcher, the search and the menu. EN / FR and your name are left out to save room: change the language in Preferences. Press Esc or click anywhere else to close an open panel (switcher, bell, cog, apps or search results). See also: Your home page, Your preferences and sign-in security, Recording your time
home: Your home page lists the engagements you work on and what is waiting for you. Who: everyone in the firm. What your home page shows When you sign in, AuditISA opens your home page, the Dashboard. It greets you by name (Welcome) and lists Your engagements. You only see the engagements whose team you belong to. An invitation to join an engagement team shows as a large card at the top of the page: You are invited to … as …, with the engagement and your role. Click Accept: the invitation opens and you accept it there (see Answering an invitation). Click Decline to say no and give a reason. Accepting means you confirm that you are independent of this client for this year. The To do card gathers what needs you across all your engagements: Working papers awaiting review, Acceptance awaiting the partner's sign-off, Overdue tasks and Significant deficiency to communicate, with the engagement each line belongs to. Click a line to go straight there. One card per engagement: the client, the period end and the kind of engagement; the current phase and its Phase deadline; Report due by; the engagement partner; and whether the acceptance is signed (Acceptance signed or Acceptance to sign). A bar and a percentage show how far the engagement file has got. Click Continue to open the engagement. An archived engagement shows Archived on a date and File locked. Click Open to read it; nothing in it can be changed. While you are on no team yet, the page says You are in the firm. Your engagements appear here once a manager adds you to a team and you accept. A partner, a manager or the firm administrator also reads Start with + New engagement. The + New engagement button appears for everyone except read-only users. Your home page lists the engagements you work on To jump between engagements, use the ENGAGEMENTS button in the top bar (Recent engagements, All engagements). The Search… box finds engagements and tasks, and also searches the methodology guidance (In the methodology) and your team's answers (In the answers). See also: The top bar, Opening a new engagement, The engagement dashboard
first-sign-in: From your invitation link to your first screen, then signing in again and recovering a forgotten password. Who: everyone in the firm. Your personal invitation link Nobody creates a password for you, and nobody sends you one. Instead, your firm administrator adds you to the firm in AuditISA and gives you a personal invitation link, usually by email or by a message. With that link you choose your own password. Nobody else ever knows it, not even the administrator or AuditISA. The link is yours alone: do not forward it. It works once. After you have set your password, it no longer opens anything. It expires after 72 hours. If it has expired, or if you lost it, ask your firm administrator for a new one: they click New link next to your name. The very first administrator of a firm receives a different link from AuditISA. It works once and expires after 72 hours. The page says Welcome, asks for a password of at least 12 characters (Password (at least 12 characters) and Repeat the password) and ends with Save and log in. Setting your password Open the invitation link in your web browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari). The page says Welcome to and the name of your firm, then Choose your password to finish setting up your account. Check that your email address is shown. It is your login name for AuditISA, and it cannot be changed on this page. Check or correct your name. Type the password you have chosen, then type it a second time to confirm it. Click Set my password. AuditISA signs you in and opens your home page. Choose your own password from your invitation link Choose a long password that you use nowhere else, for example four unrelated words. Engagement files hold your clients' confidential information. Your home page may be empty at first: it says You are in the firm. Your engagements appear here once a manager adds you to a team and you accept. Being in the firm does not open any engagement. When someone invites you to a team, a large card at the top of your home page says You are invited to … as …: click Accept (or Decline). Your invitations also wait under the cog, in My invitations, and the bell tells you when a new one arrives. Signing in later Go to your firm's AuditISA address. Save it as a bookmark the first time. Type your email address and your password. Click Log in. To leave, click Sign out at the right of the top bar. Do this every time on a shared or public computer. If you see a band reading STAGING - test data, no email at the bottom of the screen, you are on a test copy, not on your firm's real tool. Nothing you enter there counts. If you forget your password The sign-in page shows Forgot your password? under the password box only when your firm's email sending is switched on. The tool then emails you a link to choose a new password. On the sign-in page, click Forgot your password?. Enter your email address and confirm. Open the email from AuditISA and follow its link. The page says Welcome to and the name of your firm, then Choose a new password for your account. Type the new password twice, then click Save my new password. If you do not see Forgot your password?, your firm's email sending is off. Ask your firm administrator: they give you a New password link from the Users screen. It opens the same page, works once and expires after 24 hours. See also: Welcome to AuditISA, Your preferences and sign-in security, Answering an invitation, Users of the firm
preferences: Your own details, your password, your language and two-step verification at sign-in. Who: everyone in the firm, each for their own account. Two-step verification You can protect your account with a second step at sign-in: after your password, AuditISA asks for a six-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone (for example Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator). Someone who learns your password still cannot get in without your phone. Partners and administrators in particular should switch it on. Click the cog (Settings) in the top bar, then Preferences. Open the Security tab. Click the button to enable two-factor authentication and confirm your password. Scan the square code shown on screen with your authenticator app. Type the six-digit code the app shows, then confirm. API keys are switched off on every firm's server, for every user: they would let someone bypass two-step verification. Choosing your language AuditISA works in English and in French. Click EN or FR in the top bar at any time. The page reloads in that language and AuditISA keeps your choice for your next visits. New accounts start in the firm's language, which the firm administrator sets; each person then chooses their own. Your profile The right of the top bar shows your name, your role in the firm and your initials. To see or change your own details: Click the cog (Settings), then Preferences. Change what you need, for example your email signature or how you receive notifications. To change your password, open the Security tab and click Change password. You type your current password, then the new one. Click Update Preferences. Preferences: your profile, password and two-step verification If you have forgotten your password, you cannot reach this window: use Forgot your password? on the sign-in page, or ask your firm administrator for a New password link (see Signing in for the first time). You cannot change your own role. Only the firm administrator changes roles, and never their own. See also: Signing in for the first time, The top bar, Sign-off policy
firm-users: Bring your colleagues into AuditISA, give each the right role, and stop someone's access when needed. Who: the firm administrator. Partners see some of the firm settings too (see the table below). Where the firm settings are Click the cog (Settings) in the top bar. What you see depends on your role: Item under the cog What it is for Who sees it Sign-off policy The firm-wide sign-off rules Partners and the firm administrator Sign-off matrix Who prepares, reviews and signs each task Partners and the firm administrator File index The list of every task an engagement file can hold Partners and the firm administrator Audit log Every change made in the firm's engagement files Firm administrator only Users Invite people, set roles, deactivate Firm administrator only Settings Email sending status and internal projects Firm administrator only Users and Settings are also in the Apps grid (nine dots). Adding a team member to the firm Open Users. In the top box, type the person's Email and Name, and choose their Role (see the table below). To put them on an engagement team at the same time, choose the engagement in Also add to engagement, then their Team role. The list holds the open engagements whose team you are on; leave No engagement otherwise. Click Invite. A green box appears with the Invitation link. Click Copy and send the link to the person yourself, by email or a private message. When the firm's email sending is on, Send by email next to Copy sends it for you from the firm's mailbox. They choose their own password: none is created or sent. The link works once and expires after 72 hours. The person appears in the list as Invited, then Active once they have signed in, with their Last login. If their link expired or was lost, click New link on their row (only possible until they first sign in). To change a role, choose another one in their row. To stop someone's access, click Deactivate; Reactivate undoes it. Nothing they did is deleted. With an engagement chosen, the green box also says Also invited to … and They accept it after their first sign-in. The invitation waits on their home page, where they confirm their independence when they accept it. When someone forgets their password For a person who has already signed in, click New password link on their row. A green box shows the New password link: send it to the person yourself. They choose a new password: none is created or sent. The link works once and expires after 24 hours. Each new password link is written to the Administration log. Users: invite a colleague and copy their link Role What the person can do Firm administrator Everything a partner can, plus users, firm settings, the audit log and the analytics thresholds. Partner Can be the engagement partner of an engagement and give partner sign-offs; sets the sign-off rules; sees the whole firm's time reports. Manager Runs engagements, reviews work, sets time budgets; sees the whole firm's time reports. Senior Prepares work and can review the work of others, depending on your firm's sign-off policy. Staff Prepares working papers. Engagement quality reviewer Reviews the engagements they are asked to review and signs the quality review; does not change the engagement file. Read only Reads the engagement files of their teams; changes nothing. A role gives no access to an engagement: only the engagement's team does. Choose Also add to engagement when you invite someone, or the engagement partner or manager adds them to the team later. Either way, the person accepts the invitation after signing in. Some changes are refused, to protect the firm: you cannot change your own access; the firm must keep at least one active administrator; and a person who is the engagement partner of an engagement cannot be deactivated or moved below partner until that role is transferred. Further down the Users screen: Allowed email domains: one per line (for example your firm's own domain). Only addresses in these domains can be invited. Empty means no restriction. Click Save. Administration log: who invited whom (and to which engagement), role changes, new links and new password links, invitations sent by email, deactivations. A row marked Technical support shows when AuditISA support entered the firm. See also: Signing in for the first time, Firm settings and email, Sign-off policy, Your engagement team
firm-settings: The Settings screen shows whether the firm sends email and holds the internal projects people log time on. Who: the firm administrator only. Where to find it Click the cog (Settings) in the top bar, then Settings. It is also in the Apps grid (nine dots). Email sending The Settings screen shows Outgoing mail as Sending on or Sending off (on a test copy: Off on the test environment). The firm's email is set up by AuditISA when the firm is created: the firm gives AuditISA the settings of its own mailbox, the firm's server tests them without sending any message, and switches sending on only if the test passes. Nobody changes them from this screen: AuditISA sets up the firm's outgoing mail when the firm is put into service. To change it, ask AuditISA. While sending is on, the sign-in page offers Forgot your password?, and the Users screen offers Send by email next to Copy for invitation links. While it is off, AuditISA sends no email (no notices by mail, no password reset): copy the invitation and new password links and send them yourself. On the same screen you manage the Internal projects people log time on (see Recording your time). See also: Users of the firm, Signing in for the first time, Recording your time
signoff-policy: The firm-wide rules on who may review and sign, valid for every engagement. Who: partners and the firm administrator. Only they can change it. The fields of the policy Click the cog (Settings), then Sign-off policy. Field Meaning Minimum Reviewer Role The lowest rank that may review any task (default: Senior). Require Distinct Preparer Approver When ticked (the default), the same person cannot be assigned as both preparer and reviewer of a task. Allow Sole Practitioner Always off and cannot be changed. Allowed Email Domains The same list as on the Users screen. Language of the firm The language new accounts start in. Partner sign-off required on Extra tasks on which the partner must sign, on top of those the matrix already asks for. Rules fixed for every firm No self-review: whoever prepared a working paper cannot also review it; AuditISA refuses. One engagement partner per engagement: each engagement has exactly one, who must be a partner or the firm administrator. It cannot be created without one. To change partner, use the transfer form. Only the engagement partner, or the partner they delegate to, gives the partner sign-offs on that engagement. See also: Sign-off matrix, Users of the firm, Acceptance and the engagement partner
signoff-matrix: The rank needed to prepare, review and sign each task, with the firm's own rules where you set them. Who: partners and the firm administrator. Reading and setting the matrix The Sign-off matrix lists every task in audit order with the rank needed to prepare it (Minimum preparer), to review it (Minimum reviewer) and whether a Partner sign-off is needed. By default, for example, acceptance and independence tasks (P1, P2) are prepared by a manager and reviewed by a partner, and most execution tasks are prepared by staff and reviewed by a senior. To set a firm rule for one task, fill in Firm's minimum preparer, Firm's minimum reviewer or Firm's partner sign-off on its row. Blank means the firm default applies. Rows with a firm rule stand out in colour. To change many rows, click Export to Excel, fill in columns I, J and K, then click Import from Excel, choose the file and click Import. If one row is wrong, nothing is saved. The reviewer must never rank below the preparer: AuditISA raises the reviewer if needed. The sign-off matrix, with one firm rule set See also: Sign-off policy, The audit file index
file-index: The list of every task an engagement file can hold, in the order of the audit. Who: partners and the firm administrator. Reading the index Click the cog (Settings), then File index. The Audit file index lists every task an engagement file can hold, in the order of the audit: Order, code, title, section, Phase, tier (Core, Standard, Extended) and whether it is conditional. It is the same for every firm and cannot be edited here. Use the filters Core and Conditional, or group by Phase or Section. See also: Sign-off matrix, Welcome to AuditISA
audit-log: Every change made in the firm's engagement files, with who made it and when. Who: the firm administrator only. Reading the log Click the cog (Settings), then Audit log. Each line shows the Date, the User, the Engagement, the Task, a Summary, and for an answer the full text Before and After. Nobody can edit or delete it. Filter on Answer changes or Firm settings, or group by user, engagement or task. See also: Users of the firm
analytics-thresholds: How far a substantive analytical procedure's result may differ from the expectation before it must be investigated. Who: the firm administrator only. Setting the firm thresholds The thresholds are set by combined risk, as a percentage of performance materiality (ISA 520): Lower risk (%), Moderate risk (%), Higher risk (%) (defaults 75, 50 and 25). Lower risk allows the widest gap. Open an engagement's tools, then Substantive analytics. Click Firm thresholds. Change the three figures and click Save. Only procedures saved after the change use the new figures. See also: Analytics and the data tools, Materiality
clients: The firm's list of clients: find a client, create a new one, or retire one you no longer act for. Who: anyone in the firm can read client records. Staff, seniors and managers can create a new client. Only a partner or the firm administrator can change or archive an existing one. Where to find your clients A client record is held once for the whole firm, not per engagement. Everyone in the firm can read it, but each engagement for that client is still visible only to its own team. Click the cog (Settings) in the top bar. Click Clients. The list shows each client's Name, Legal Form, Sector and Registration Number. To find a client, type in the search box. The search looks at the name, the registration number and the NIU (the tax identification number). From inside an engagement, the link About the client → under the engagement title opens that client's record directly. The firm's client list Creating a client Create the client before you open its first engagement: the New engagement form asks you to choose an existing client. In the Clients list, click New. Type the client's Name as it appears in its articles of association. Choose the Legal Form (for example SA with a board of directors, SARL, SAS or GIE). Fill in the other fields you know now (see The client record). Only the name, the legal form and the reporting framework are required. Click the save icon (the cloud) at the top of the form. A client record Retiring a client A client record is never deleted, because past engagement files refer to it. When you no longer act for a client, a partner archives the record instead. Open the client record. Click the gear icon Actions at the top of the form, then Archive. An archived client shows a red Archived ribbon and no longer appears in the list. To see it again, open the search options and choose the Archived filter. Unarchive in the same menu brings it back. See also: The client record, Opening a new engagement
client-record: What each field of a client record is for, and how to keep the record up to date from one year to the next. Who: anyone in the firm can read a client record. Only a partner or the firm administrator can change an existing one. What each field is for Field What to enter, and why it matters Name The legal name. It appears on the dashboard, the reports and the letters. Legal Form SA (board of directors), SA (administrateur général), SARL, SAS, GIE or Other. Some legal tasks depend on it: for example, one of the OHADA legal procedures does not apply to an SARL or a GIE. Sector The client's main activity (trade, services, financial, energy and so on). Reporting framework Revised SYSCOHADA, normal system. It is the only framework offered today and is filled in for you. A new engagement takes it from the client. Governance Mode How the entity is run: a board with a combined chairman and managing director, a board with a separate managing director, a sole director, or management by gérant(s). Regulator The sector regulator, if any (for example COBAC for banks or CIMA for insurers). Registration Number and NIU The trade register number and the tax identification number. Both can be searched. Address The registered office address. Share capital (FCFA) Used by the check of equity against half of the share capital in the OHADA legal work. If you leave it empty, the tool looks for the capital in the trial balance. Mandate Type and Mandate Start Year Whether you were appointed by the statutes (2 financial years) or by the general meeting (6 financial years), and the first year. They let the tool work out when your mandate ends. Listed, Joint auditor (co-CAC), Public interest entity Tick the boxes that apply. They record the client's status. Listed and Joint auditor (co-CAC) are also used when the audit report is issued: for a listed client, key audit matters are required. Ticking Listed or Public interest entity here does not set how complex the engagement is. That is decided only by the answers to the engagement questionnaire (see The engagement questionnaire). A client record Keeping the record up to date Review the client record at the start of each year, before you open the new engagement. Changes of share capital, governance or regulator are common and some tasks rely on them. Open the client from the Clients list. Change the fields you need. Only a partner or the firm administrator can save a change. Click the save icon. If you change the client's name, the new name is used everywhere at once, including on past engagements. See also: Your clients, Opening a new engagement
new-engagement: Open a new engagement for a client: its name, nature, period, engagement partner and report language. Who: any member of the firm except a read-only user can open an engagement. The engagement partner must be a partner or the firm administrator. Opening the engagement On the Dashboard, click + New engagement. Choose the Client. If it is not in the list, create it first (see Your clients). Type an Engagement name, for example "Statutory audit 2025". Choose the Nature of the service: Statutory audit or Non-statutory audit. A non-statutory audit leaves out the OHADA tasks that only a statutory auditor performs. Choose the Engagement partner. Check the period: Audit period from and to. The Financial year follows the end date. Choose the Report language, English or French. It is the language of the report, the letters, the legal documents and the exports of this engagement. Click Create. Opening a new engagement The engagement partner joins the team at once. If you are a staff member, senior or manager, you join the team too, in your own role. A partner who opens an engagement for another partner is not added to it, and so cannot open it afterwards unless invited. The window warns you before you click Create: You will not be on this engagement's team. To open it later, ask … to add you. No question about the client's profile is asked in this window. The questionnaire opens straight after Create. See also: The engagement questionnaire · Your engagement team
engagement-questionnaire: Answer the engagement questionnaire: AuditISA works out the level of the engagement and the tasks it needs. Who: any member of the engagement team except a read-only user. The engagement quality reviewer can read the answers but not change them. Answering the engagement questionnaire The Engagement profile screen asks 19 questions in seven sections: The entity, The business, IT, Specialists, people and ownership, How the evidence will be obtained, Risk, and Approach and history. Click a section on the left, or use Next section and Previous. Click one answer for each question. Some answers open a follow-up question just below (for example, a parent company is asked whether it consolidates). Watch the panel on the right: it shows the Level so far, marked Provisional, the reasons under Why, and the tasks Added by your answers:. When all 19 questions are answered, click Conclude. The tasks are put on the engagement file. Until then the button is greyed and the line under it counts what is missing: Answer … more questions to conclude. (or Answer 1 more question to conclude.). Click See the tasks to open the task list. Answers are saved automatically. You can leave with Back to the engagement and come back later. Until you conclude, the dashboard shows Profile not finished: finish it to get your tasks. with a Finish the profile → link. The engagement questionnaire and its live panel There is no "don't know" answer: every question must be answered before you can conclude. If you do not yet know, find out from the client first. How the answers decide the level The level is worked out from the answers alone. Nobody can change it by hand. The answers are read in two steps. Level When What the engagement file holds Complex Any one sign of complexity: listed (question 1); a bank, insurer or other public-interest entity (question 2); controls testing required by law (question 3); a parent whose components other auditors audit (question 4); more than 3 activities or sites (questions 5 and 6); a major change this year (question 7); any IT point rated High (question 8); specialists needed on the core of the business (question 9). Full ISAs and the full methodology: all task templates. Non-complex No sign of complexity, but at least one Very simple condition is not met: for example a regulator receives the accounts, fraud is suspected, an owner is unknown, a going-concern doubt, significant related-party dealings, complex estimates, or an approach other than testing balances at year end. A scaled engagement file: core and standard task templates. Very simple No sign of complexity and every Very simple condition met. The shortest engagement file: core task templates only, fully substantive, all at year end. For a Non-complex or Very simple engagement whose period starts on or after 15 December 2025, the panel notes that the engagement file may be documented under the ISA for Less Complex Entities. Facts decide the tasks, the level decides the depth Two separate things shape your engagement file. The level decides how deep the work is documented. The facts decide whether a task applies at all, whatever the level. For example: A first-year audit (question 19) adds P1.2, contact with the predecessor auditor. Specialists, tax included (question 9), add S5.1, reliance on experts. Books or key data kept by someone outside the entity (question 14) add S5.2, service organisations. Using internal audit's work (question 18) adds S5.3, internal audit. Known or suspected fraud (question 11) keeps the fraud and laws work (P5.1, E3.1, E6.1) on the engagement file. Answers only ever add tasks. If you change an answer after concluding, the level is worked out again and any new task is added; no task is removed. See also: Opening a new engagement · Acceptance and the engagement partner · The engagement dashboard
acceptance: The first phase of a new engagement: decide to take on or keep the client, then move the engagement to planning. Who: the engagement team prepares the acceptance tasks; the engagement partner signs P1.1 and moves the engagement to planning. Only the engagement partner or the firm administrator can transfer the partner role. Acceptance and continuance The new engagement starts in the Acceptance phase. Its first group of tasks, Acceptance and continuance (P1), covers the decision to take on or keep the client: the acceptance or continuance checklist (P1.1), the predecessor auditor (P1.2, first year only), the preconditions for an audit (P1.3), the engagement letter (P1.4) and the decision on an engagement quality review (P1.5). The independence conclusion sits in P2.1. The engagement can move to planning only when: P1.1 is complete and concluded "accept"; every required acceptance check is answered "yes"; the engagement partner has signed P1.1; exactly one engagement partner has accepted; the review notes on P1 are cleared. Until then, the home page shows Acceptance to sign on the engagement card. Then the engagement partner clicks Advance to planning on the Engagement record. The engagement partner Each engagement has exactly one engagement partner, who must be a partner or the firm administrator. The partner gives the partner sign-offs on the key working papers and has the last word on the engagement. To hand the role to another partner, open the Engagement record (gear icon) and click Transfer the partner role. Choose the New engagement partner and the Outgoing partner's new role, then Transfer. Only the engagement partner or the firm administrator can do this. The engagement partner may name a Partner delegate on the same record: another partner on the team who can give the partner sign-offs in their place. See also: Your engagement team · The engagement dashboard
engagement-team: Only the people on an engagement's team can open it: see who they are, invite a colleague, change a role or take someone off the team. Who: a manager, a partner or the firm administrator who is on the team can invite members and change roles. Only a partner can give or take away the engagement partner role. The engagement quality reviewer cannot change the team. Seeing who is on the team Open the engagement. Click the tools icon (the four squares, Engagement tools) in the top bar. Click the Engagement team tile. The list shows each member, their Email, Role and Status (Invited, Accepted or Declined), with the dates Invited on and Answered on. The Engagement team tile Inviting a member In the Engagement team list, click Invite a member. (On the Engagement record, the button is called Invite to the team.) Type the person's Email. Only people already in the firm can be invited (see below). Choose the Team Role: Staff, Senior, Manager, Senior manager, Director, Partner or Engagement quality reviewer. Click Invite. The person sees the invitation in three places: the bell (Notifications), a large card at the top of their home page (You are invited to … as …, with Accept and Decline), and My invitations. No email is sent at this stage. Inviting a colleague The window reminds you: Only people already in the firm can be invited. Someone new is added first by the firm administrator, on the Users screen. If you type the address of someone who is not in the firm yet, a message titled Not possible yet says This person is not in the firm yet. Ask your firm administrator to add them first (Users screen); they can add them to this engagement at the same time. The firm administrator does both in one step, with Also add to engagement (see Users of the firm). Invitations go only to email addresses on the firm's allowed domains. The firm administrator keeps that list. Nobody gets a new account from this window: only the firm administrator adds people to the firm. Rules on roles Role Rule Partner One engagement partner per engagement, who must be a partner or the firm administrator. To change who holds it, use Transfer the partner role (see Acceptance and the engagement partner). Engagement quality reviewer Must be a partner or hold the firm role of engagement quality reviewer. They must not be on the team in another role, and must not have been engagement partner of the same client in the two years before this period end (the cooling-off period of ISQM 2). Tick Objectivity declaration to appoint them. Appointing one adds task C4.2 to the engagement file. Others Any member of the firm from an allowed domain. A role on the team does not change the person's firm role. Changing a role In the Engagement team list, click the member's Role and choose another. The role cell is open only to a manager or above, on an engagement that is not archived. The engagement partner's role cannot be changed this way: transfer it instead. Removing someone from the team Open the Engagement record from the gear icon. Go to the Team tab. Click the bin icon at the end of the member's line, then save. The tasks that person was preparing, reviewing or assigned to go back to unassigned, and the dashboard warns that tasks have no preparer. The removal is written to the activity trail. The engagement partner cannot be removed while they are the only partner: transfer the role first. Nobody can change the team of an archived engagement. The engagement file is locked. See also: Answering an invitation · Acceptance and the engagement partner · The engagement dashboard
my-invitations: Accept or decline an invitation to join an engagement team. Who: any member of the firm who has been invited to an engagement team. Answering an invitation On your home page, click Accept on the invitation card (You are invited to … as …): the invitation opens. You can also click the gear icon (Settings), then My invitations, and open the invitation, or click it in the bell. The invitation It shows the Engagement name, the Client, the Fiscal year and your role. Click Accept, or click Decline and give a Reason. Accepting an invitation By accepting, you confirm that you are independent of this client for this year. If you have any doubt about your independence (a family link, a financial interest, a past role at the client), speak to the engagement partner before you accept. Until you accept, you cannot open the engagement. A decline and its reason are written to the engagement's activity trail, so the partner knows why. The independence conclusion for the whole engagement is documented on task P2.1. The firm's yearly independence declarations are collected outside AuditISA. See also: Your engagement team · Notifications
engagement-dashboard: The engagement dashboard shows how far each phase has gone and what is waiting for you on this engagement. Who: every member of the engagement team. Phases, groups and tasks Inside an engagement, the top bar shows the four phases, Planning, Strategy and risks, Execution and Conclusion, then Tasks. The dashboard shows the OVERALL COMPLETION and one ring per phase. Click a ring. The groups of that phase open below it, each with tasks done out of tasks in total. Click a group to see its Task list. Click a task to open its working paper. The engagement dashboard Below the rings you find: a warning such as 3 tasks have no preparer. with Assign them →; REQUIRES YOUR ATTENTION: overdue tasks, each with its delay; My tasks (open and mine), each marked To prepare, In progress, To review or To sign. When nothing is yours, the tile says why, for example Nothing is assigned to you yet. Ask the manager to set you as preparer. (see The Tasks screen and deadlines); Review notes and findings: Notes for me, Notes by me, Deficiencies and Misstatements; Calendar: the next deadlines, with a red count of overdue ones. The engagement file index by phase Phase Groups Planning P1 Acceptance and continuance · P2 Independence and team · P3 Understanding the business · P4 Entity-level controls and IT · P5 Fraud risks and team discussion · P6 Materiality and significant accounts · P7 Planning review and approval Strategy and risks S1 Transactions, flows and walkthroughs · S2 Controls and IT · S3 Combined risk assessment · S4 Specific risk areas · S5 Audit procedure design · S6 Audit strategy memorandum Execution E1 Tests of controls · E2 Control updates · E4 Substantive procedures · E5 Specific procedures · E6 Registers, opening balances and revaluation Conclusion C1 Summary of audit differences · C2 Final review of the financial statements · C3 Representations · C4 Review and approval · C5 Statutory reports · C5 Communications and legal procedures · C6 Documentation and archiving Which tasks are on your engagement file depends on the engagement questionnaire (see The engagement questionnaire). Under a group's task list, Conditional papers lists tasks that are Not counted: they come onto the file when their trigger answers yes. The "Statutory reports" heading In the Conclusion phase, the reports the law asks of the statutory auditor sit together under Statutory reports: the opinion and auditor's report (C5.1), the special report on regulated agreements (C5.3), the Article 715 report (C5.4) and the Article 525 certification (C5.10). Each stays a separate task with its own sign-offs. The other letters and legal procedures are under Communications and legal procedures. See also: The Tasks screen and deadlines · Notifications · Your home page
tasks: The Tasks screen lists every task of the engagement, with who prepares, reviews and signs it, its due date and its status. Who: every member of the engagement team. A senior or above can set a task's deadline. The Tasks screen Click Tasks in the top bar to see every task of the engagement in one table. Use the filters Mine, All and Open; each shows its count. When nothing is yours, Mine says why. While the engagement questionnaire is not concluded, the engagement has no tasks yet: No tasks yet: the partner has answered … of … questions in the engagement questionnaire. Once it is concluded: Nothing is assigned to you yet. Ask the manager to set you as preparer. All the tasks of an engagement The PREPARER, REVIEWER and PARTNER columns carry a small letter (P, R, A). It is grey until that person has signed. Status Meaning NOT STARTED Nobody has worked on the working paper yet. IN PROGRESS The preparer has started. IN REVIEW The preparer has signed; the reviewer's turn. TO SIGN The reviewer has signed; waiting for the partner's sign-off. COMPLETE Every required signature is given. NOT APPLICABLE Marked not applicable, with a reason. Deadlines and late flags Each task has one due date. A senior or above can set it in the Assignment panel of the working paper (Deadline). Without one, the deadline of its phase applies: Phase Deadline Acceptance 90 days before the period end Planning 45 days before the period end Execution 90 days after the period end Conclusion 150 days after the period end Report Due 6 months after the period end An open task past its date shows Overdue by and the number of days, in red. Late flags stop once an engagement is archived. See also: The engagement dashboard · Working on a working paper
notifications: The bell in the top bar tells you what is new for you. Who: everyone, for their own notifications. The bell The bell in the top bar counts what is new for you: a working paper To review or To sign after a colleague's signature, a Task assigned to you, or an Invitation to a team. Click a line to open the task. See all notifications opens the full list. See also: The engagement dashboard · Answering an invitation
file-scope: Move an engagement opened before 17 November 2026 to the current task scope. Who: a partner on the team (not the engagement quality reviewer). Applying the current task scope Engagements opened before 17 November 2026 keep the tasks they were opened with: no task appears or disappears on a live engagement by itself. To move such an engagement to the current scope: Open the Engagement record from the gear icon. Click Apply the current task scope and confirm. Tasks the current scope adds come onto the engagement file. Tasks that hold no work and no longer apply are hidden. Tasks that hold work stay. The result is written to the activity trail. The button disappears once applied. See also: The engagement questionnaire · The engagement dashboard
uploading-data: Upload the client's own figures (trial balance, ledger, payroll and others) so that the tools can work on them. Who: any team member except a read-only user can upload. Everyone on the team can read the uploads. Where to upload Open the engagement and click the tools icon (Engagement tools) in the top bar. Click the Data analytics tile. A second page of tiles opens, one per kind of data. Click the tile you need, for example Trial balance analyzer or Payroll analyzer. Click Import a trial balance (trial balance) or Import a dataset (all others). Each tile offers Download the template: an Excel file with the expected columns. Send it to the client to save time at matching. What you can upload Files are accepted as .csv or .xlsx. Mandatory columns are needed for the import; the others are optional and make the analysis richer. Kind of data Mandatory columns Some optional columns Trial balance Account; then either debit and credit movements, or closing debit and credit, or one signed closing column Description, opening balances General ledger Account number, journal entry number, transaction description, amount (or debit and credit), journal date Account name, journal code, reference, third party, cost centre, recorded / prepared / approved by Receivables Customer number and name, invoice reference, invoice date, transaction amount Transaction type, customer location, payment terms Payables Supplier number and name, transaction reference, transaction date, transaction amount Transaction type, supplier location, payment terms Fixed assets Asset number, description, cost, category, acquisition date, depreciation rate Accumulated depreciation, net book value, accounts, movements of the year, disposals Inventory Item number, item description, quantity, unit price, amount Location Payroll Employee number, employee name, gross pay Net pay Bank statements Date, description, amount Supplier statements Supplier number, amount Supplier name Optional payroll columns The payroll upload accepts 13 more columns. None is required, and each is marked Improves the analysis on the matching screen, where a line shows how many were matched (for example 5 of 13 matched). The more you provide, the more the payroll analytical review can compare with the prior year: gross pay, headcount, components of pay, joiners and leavers, average pay and taxes on pay. In the downloadable template these column titles are shaded. Optional column What it gives the analysis Employee category or grade; Department Pay and headcount by group Hire date; Leaving date Joiners and leavers of the year Base salary; Allowances and bonuses; Benefits in kind; Overtime The components of pay Income tax withheld; Social security, employee share; Social security, employer share; Other employer charges Taxes and charges on pay, to agree with the returns Month or period Monthly trend of the payroll Importing a file, step by step The import has three steps. Nothing is saved until you click Import at the end. 1 Upload Check the Kind of data. Choose the Timing (see the table below). Choose the file in File (.csv, .xlsx). Leave The first line holds the column titles ticked if it does. Click Read the file. 2 Match the columns Each line is one column of the client's file: Column in your file, its First three values, and the AuditISA field it feeds. How it was matched reads Matched automatically, Chosen by you or Not recognised. Check each automatic match. To change one, open the list in AuditISA field and choose another field, or Do not import. Make sure every field marked mandatory has a column. The message at the top tells you what is still missing. If dates or amounts look wrong, set the Decimal separator, Date format, Column separator or Sheet. For a general ledger without a single entry number, use Entry identified by several columns. Click Check the file. Matching the file's columns Leave Remember this matching for this client's next file of this kind ticked. Next year the same layout is matched for you. 3 Check The tool reads every row and shows the rows read, the totals and, for a ledger, whether debits equal credits. Each point found is marked Left out, Imported with a warning or Blocks the import. If you see The file can be imported., click Import. If not, correct the file or click Back to matching. A general ledger whose debits and credits do not balance is refused. Ask the client for a complete extract rather than editing it yourself. Timing and uploads for next year Timing Use it for Pre-audit The client's figures before your adjustments. A pre-audit trial balance drives the engagement file (lead schedules, materiality, significant accounts). Post-audit The figures after the adjustments agreed. Prior year Last year's figures, for comparisons. Subsequent period (next year) Data of the year after the one audited, for the cut-off procedures and the search for unrecorded liabilities. It never stands in for the year audited. A next-year ledger covering fewer than 30 days after the year end is too short for cut-off work. See also: Versions of an upload · Analytics and the data tools
data-versions: Every upload is kept: see which one the work rests on, and delete an upload made by mistake. Who: any team member except a read-only user can delete an upload. Everyone on the team can read the uploads. Versions Every upload is kept. For each kind and timing, the latest upload is the one In use; an earlier one shows Superseded on and stays in the list as a record. The list also shows Imported on, Imported by, the File, the Rows and the Total amount, so you can always tell which file the work rests on. Uploads and their versions Deleting an upload Click the bin icon (Delete this upload) at the end of the line, or the button of the same name on the upload. Read the confirmation: it says what will be removed and which earlier upload, if any, takes over. Click Delete, or Keep it to cancel. If you delete the upload in use, the previous one of the same kind and timing is in use again. See also: Uploading the client's data
timesheet: Enter your hours on engagements and internal projects, and submit your week before the deadline. Who: everyone enters their own hours. Partners and the firm administrator can reopen a locked week. Opening your timesheet There are three ways in: Click the clock in the top bar (shown when you are not inside an engagement). Open the Apps grid (nine dots) and click Timesheet. Inside an engagement, click the cog and choose Log time on this engagement. That engagement is then already chosen for you. The Timesheet page shows one week, Monday to Sunday. Use the arrows to go to the Previous week or the Next week, and This week to come back. Back to the audit returns you to your engagements. Where you can charge time The Engagement or project list has two parts: My engagements: only the engagements whose team you belong to and have accepted. You cannot charge time to an engagement you have not been invited to, and an archived engagement takes no more hours. Internal projects: the firm's own work, such as Training, Leave and Administration. The firm administrator adds or archives these under Settings. Everyone enters their own hours only. Nobody can enter time for someone else. Entering hours Choose the Date (today or an earlier day of the week shown; future days are not offered). Choose the Engagement or project. If you wish, choose the Task (optional) you worked on. Leave it at None otherwise. Type the Hours, for example 2.5. Add a short Note if it helps your manager understand the time. Click Charge. The message Hours charged. confirms it, and the hours appear in the week's grid. You can also correct hours straight in the grid: click a day's box on a row, change the figure and click elsewhere. The grid shows a total per row, per day and for the week. Hours must be between 0 and 24, and a day cannot add up to more than 24 hours. Your week: enter hours, check the totals, submit Submitting your week When the week is complete, click Submit the week. The status changes to Submitted and the page shows when you submitted it. If you notice a mistake, click Take back, correct it and submit again. You can do this until the deadline. The deadline for a week is the Tuesday after it, at 23:59, Douala time. The page always shows it (Deadline: …, Douala time), and a yellow line reminds you when last week still waits to be submitted. Status What it means Open You can enter and change hours. Submitted Sent; take it back before the deadline to change it. Locked, submitted Submitted and the deadline has passed: final. Locked, not submitted The deadline passed before you submitted: the week is now read only. Reopened A partner or the firm administrator reopened it for you, for 48 hours. Not started A week still to come. Weeks you missed are listed under Overdue, not submitted. Click one to open it. Enter your hours each evening and submit every Friday. Time reports and budgets depend on complete weeks. Reopening a locked week Who: the firm administrator, or a partner of one of the person's engagements. Ask a partner or your firm administrator; you cannot reopen your own week. They open Reports on the Timesheet page and, under Reopen a locked week: Choose the Person. Type A date of the week (DD/MM/YYYY). Give a Written reason (at least 10 characters). Click Reopen for 48 hours. Each reopening is kept in a list with the reason, who reopened it and until when. The person then has 48 hours to complete and submit the week. See also: Time reports · Budget and actual · Firm settings and email
time-reports: Follow the hours recorded, by person, by engagement or by week. Who: the firm administrator, partners and managers see the whole firm; a quality reviewer sees the engagements they review; everyone else sees their own hours. Reading the time reports Click Reports on the Timesheet page. The line under Time reports tells you what you can see: Your role What the report covers Firm administrator, partner, manager The whole firm Quality reviewer on an engagement Your hours and the team's on the engagements you review Everyone else Your hours Type the period in From and To (DD/MM/YYYY) and click Show. Choose By person, By engagement or By week. For your own analysis, click Pivot table, or Excel export to download the figures with every line in detail. Time reports, seen by a partner See also: Recording your time · Budget and actual
budget: Compare the hours charged on an engagement with its budget, per person and per phase. Who: the partner or manager of the team sees every member and types the budget; other team members see their own row only. Reading the budget Inside an engagement, click the cog and choose Budget and actual. Each cell reads actual hours / budget hours, per person and per phase (Planning, Strategy and risks, Execution, Conclusion). Figures over budget show in red. The partner or manager of the team sees every member and types the budget hours in the boxes. Other team members see their own row only. Hours charged to a task count in that task's phase. Hours without a task count in the phase the engagement was in on that day. Choosing the task keeps the budget follow-up accurate. See also: Recording your time · Time reports
planning: What the Planning phase holds, the tools that do the figures for you, and the order in which to work so that each step has what it needs. Who: the whole engagement team prepares; a partner approves materiality. What the Planning phase holds Inside an engagement, click Planning in the top bar. The dashboard shows the ring Planning and Risk Identification with its percentage done. Click the ring to see its groups of tasks (the working papers whose codes start with P) and how many are finished in each. Group Working papers What you do there Acceptance and continuance P1.1 to P1.5 Accept or continue the client, preconditions, engagement letter, quality review decision. Independence and team P2.1 to P2.3 Independence conclusion, team skills, group audit scope where it applies. Understanding the business P3.1, P3.2 The entity and its environment; analytical procedures used to find risks. Entity-level controls and IT P4.1 to P4.3 Controls at entity level, the control environment and the IT environment. Fraud risks and team discussion P5.1, P5.2 Fraud risks (ISA 240) and the team discussion. Materiality and significant accounts P6.1, P6.2 Set materiality; decide which accounts are significant and their relevant assertions. Planning review and approval P7.1, P7.2 Review and approval of the planning. Some working papers only appear when something on the engagement calls for them (for example P2.3 for a group audit). Each working paper has a Tools panel on the right. Its buttons open the tool that does the work for that working paper. When a tool already holds the answer, the step on the working paper says from the tool and is filled for you. You still write your own conclusion on the working paper. The order to work in The planning tools feed each other. Follow this order and nothing will be empty when you open it: Import and check the trial balance of the year (and the prior year). Without a valid trial balance, the tools below have no figures. Look at the Financial analysis and the Analytical procedures (P3.2) to spot unusual movements. Set and get approval for Materiality (P6.1). Decide the Significant accounts and their relevant assertions (P6.2). This uses the approved materiality. Move on to Strategy and risks: the combined risk assessment only lists the accounts marked significant. You can open every tool from the working paper's Tools panel, or from the Engagement tools button (the grid icon in the top bar), which shows all the tools of the engagement as tiles. See also: Uploading the client's data · Financial analysis and analytical procedures · Materiality · Significant accounts · The Strategy and risks phase
materiality: Set overall materiality, performance materiality and the clearly trivial threshold, and keep every version with its approval. Who: the engagement team prepares a version; a partner approves it. Setting materiality (P6.1) The Materiality page shows three cards: Overall materiality, Performance materiality and Clearly trivial misstatements. Below them you see the Trial balance bases (the possible benchmarks, worked out from the trial balance), your justification, and the Version history. Click Generate a version. Choose the benchmark (Profit before tax, Revenue, Total assets, Equity or Total expenses), check the Base amount and type the Percentage. If last year's engagement exists, a blue line reminds you of Last year's basis. Check Performance % (75 by default) and Clearly trivial % (5 by default). If you change the performance percentage, explain why. Write the Justification. It is required: the tool never fills in a stock sentence for you. If your percentage is outside the usual range for that benchmark, or your base amount does not match the trial balance, fill Why it departs from the range or the trial balance base. Click Generate. The new version is saved as a draft. Approval A partner then clicks Approve the latest version. Only an approved version counts: until the partner approves a new draft, the earlier approved version stays in force, and a yellow banner says so. Approved materiality feeds P6.1, P6.2 and the summary of audit differences (C1.1). Click Export to Excel for a workbook copy. If you revise materiality later, the new version needs approval again, and the trail notes that work done under the earlier figure needs review. Materiality: one approved version in force, every change kept. See also: The Planning phase · Significant accounts · The summary of audit differences
financial-analysis: Ratios and year-on-year comparisons worked out from the trial balance, to spot unusual movements. Who: the engagement team. Financial analysis Financial analysis lists the ratios worked out from the trial balance, grouped under Liquidity, Activity, Profitability, Leverage and Investment. Each row shows the current year, the prior year and the Change. Click the commentary cell (Click to type a commentary) to explain a ratio that moved. Analytical procedures (P3.2) Analytical procedures (P3.2) compares the current year with the prior year by lead schedule. A movement above performance materiality is flagged for you to consider. From there, Lead schedules and commentary opens the detail by account, and Financial analysis opens the ratios. Write your expectation on P3.2 before you open the figures. The working paper asks for it, and it makes the comparison meaningful. See also: The Planning phase · Materiality · Significant accounts
significant-accounts: Decide, lead index by lead index, which accounts are significant and their relevant assertions. Who: the engagement team. Significant accounts (P6.2) The Significant accounts page has one row per lead index (for example UA Revenue). For each row you see the Current year, the Prior year, the Variance and Variance %, whether the balance is Above threshold, and, when the general ledger is imported, how many Transactions, Preparers and Reviewers it holds. At the top, set Flag a significant movement: a percentage and an amount in FCFA, joined by and (both limits passed) or or (either one). The defaults are 10% and 10,000,000 FCFA with and. Flagged rows are counted next to a flag icon. A new account with no prior-year balance counts as above the percentage. In the Risks column, pick from the engagement's risk register the risks that bear on the account. Any live risk linked locks the row at Significant. Check the Status the tool proposes (Significant or Not significant). Change it in the cell if your judgement differs. When you depart from the proposed status, write the Reason. A departure without a reason shows in red. Tick the relevant assertions in the Relevant assertions column for every significant account. The presumed risk of fraud in revenue is linked to revenue (UA) automatically, so revenue stays significant until a partner approves a rebuttal in the risk register. An account excluded here is not worked later, so document an exclusion as carefully as an inclusion. Use Export to Excel and Import from Excel to work offline. Carried from shows decisions brought over from last year's engagement. Significant accounts: movements flagged, risks linked, decision and reason per index. See also: Materiality · The risk register · The combined risk assessment
strategy: What the Strategy and risks phase holds, the order to work in, and how your decision to rely on controls shapes the rest of the engagement file. Who: the team prepares; a partner approves rebuttals of the presumed revenue-fraud risk and risks added after planning, depending on your firm's sign-off policy. What the phase holds Click Strategy and risks in the top bar. The ring Strategy and Risk Assessment holds the working papers whose codes start with S: Transactions, flows and walkthroughs (S1), Controls and IT (S2), Combined risk assessment (S3), Specific risk areas (S4), Audit procedure design (S5) and Audit strategy memorandum (S6). Work in this order: risk register, classes of transactions, IT and close process, combined risk assessment, then procedure design (described in Procedure design). Deciding to rely on controls The tasks about testing controls (S2.1 to S2.5, E1.1, E1.2 and E2.1) come onto the engagement file only when your strategy relies on controls. They appear by themselves as soon as you do any one of these: set a class of transactions to the Controls strategy; choose Rely on any assertion of the combined risk assessment; choose one of the two relying strategies for an IT application. If you stay fully substantive, those tasks stay off the engagement file and you are not asked to complete them. The controls tasks (S2.1 to S2.5, E1.1, E1.2 and E2.1) follow your strategy. While you rely on controls they stay on the engagement file. When nothing relies on controls any more, an empty controls task leaves the engagement file, and a task that already holds work stays readable, marked Not applicable with the reason “The strategy no longer relies on controls”. If you rely on controls again, the tasks come back with their earlier work. Both moves are recorded in the activity trail. See also: The Planning phase · The Execution phase and tests of controls
risk-register: Record every risk of the engagement, link it to the accounts it affects and to the work that answers it. Who: the engagement team records the risks; a partner approves a rebuttal of the presumed revenue-fraud risk and any risk added after planning, depending on your firm's sign-off policy. The risk register (S3.1) The Risk register (S3.1) lists every risk of the engagement: its category (Business, Fraud or Error), its level (Financial statements or Assertion), its inherent rating, whether it is significant, the lead indexes it touches and its status (Identified, Response planned, Response executed, Concluded). Click Add a risk, describe it and rate its likelihood and magnitude. Open the risk and click Link to a lead index to say which accounts and assertions it affects. The link also appears in the Risks column of Significant accounts. Click Link a program step to show how the risk is answered. The presumed risks Two presumed risks are on every engagement: Revenue fraud and Management override. Management override cannot be rebutted. To rebut the revenue-fraud risk, a team member clicks Propose a rebuttal and writes why; a partner then clicks Approve the rebuttal or Reject the rebuttal. The person who proposed cannot approve their own proposal, so a second person always checks this judgement (ISA 240). A risk added once planning is closed needs a partner to click Approve the addition. See also: Significant accounts · The combined risk assessment · The Strategy and risks phase
transactions-controls: Record each class of transactions with its lead indexes, what can go wrong, its controls and its walkthrough. Who: the engagement team; each class of transactions can be assigned to one team member. Classes of transactions, what can go wrong and controls Open Transactions and controls (S1.1 to S2.2). The page shows one card per class of transactions (sales, purchases, payroll and so on): green when complete, amber to finish, red not started. A warning lists any significant account not yet covered by a class. Click New class of transactions. Give its name, type (Routine, Non-routine or Estimation), the IT applications it uses (separate them with commas) and its Strategy: Controls or Substantive. Click Assign the class to give it to a team member. Tab 1 Lead indexes: click Link a lead index and tick the assertions. Tab 2 What can go wrong: click Add what can go wrong for each risk in the flow, with its assertions. Tab 3 Controls: click Add a control. Record its owner, type (Manual, IT-dependent manual, Automated), frequency, Reliance (Normal or Heavy / significant risk), design and whether it is implemented. Tick To test for each control you will test. The grid Which control answers which risk links controls to risks: click a cell to link or unlink. Tab 4 Walkthrough: describe the flow (Initiation, Recording, Processing, Reporting, people, documents, systems), then the walkthrough itself, from Transaction selected to the conclusion. The panel beside the tabs holds the documents of the class (flowcharts, procedure manuals). One class of transactions: lead indexes, risks, controls and walkthrough in four tabs. See also: The Strategy and risks phase · IT applications and the close process · Procedure design
it-close: Record each IT application with its strategy and conclusion, and document the financial statement close process. Who: the engagement team. IT applications and IT controls IT applications and IT controls (S2.3 to S2.5) lists every application named on your classes of transactions. For each, record its Layers (application, database, operating system), a strategy and a note: Rely on the IT processes: test the IT general controls Test the automated controls directly, each period Fully substantive: no reliance on the IT controls When the work is done, click Record the S2.5 conclusion: Support reliance, Do not support reliance or Mixed. This conclusion feeds the combined risk assessment. The close process Close process (S1.4) is a form in four parts: A. The critical path of the close, B. What can go wrong, C. Changes and communications, D. Strategy and confirmation. See also: Classes of transactions and controls · The combined risk assessment · The Strategy and risks phase
combined-risk: Assess inherent risk and control risk for each relevant assertion of each significant account. Who: the engagement team. The combined risk assessment (S3.1) The Combined risk assessment (S3.1) lists only the significant accounts and only their relevant assertions. If the page is empty, it tells you what is missing: a valid trial balance, approved materiality, or accounts marked significant. For each assertion, choose Inherent risk (Lower or Higher) and Control risk (Rely or Not rely). The tool shows its suggestion and works out the Combined level (Minimal, Low, Moderate, High) and the sampling level. When you differ from the suggestion, write the Basis / reason. Tick Show only what is still to assess to see what is left. Each click saves at once: there is no Save button. Significant risks in the register that are linked to no account are listed at the bottom so none is forgotten. Rely needs a tested control covering that assertion and IT general controls that support reliance, or a written control risk basis. Once planning is closed, changing an assessment asks for a reason (E6.8). Combined risk assessment: one click per choice, saved at once. See also: Significant accounts · The risk register · The Strategy and risks phase · Procedure design
execution: What the Execution phase holds, the order to work in, and how to test the controls you rely on. Who: the team performs the work. Roles that only read (for example the quality reviewer) see every page in read-only mode. What the phase holds Click Execution in the top bar. The ring Execution holds Tests of controls (E1), Control updates (E2), Substantive procedures (E4 and E5), Specific procedures (E3, E6) and Registers, opening balances (E6). Journal entry testing (E3.1) sits in the specific procedures group under its own code. Clicking Substantive procedures opens the Substantive procedures page directly, not a task list. The figure in brackets beside it shows how many accounts are designed in S5.5. Work in this order: design the procedures, draw the samples, perform the work account by account, then record the conclusions. Tests of controls (E1.2) On the Sampling page, the Controls to test section lists every control ticked To test. Enter the Occurrences in the year on the control, then click Draw the sample. Test the occurrences drawn. Click Import the test grid (columns: reference, date, description, then one column per attribute with pass, fail or na), or Record a test one at a time. Read the Operating conclusion. If a tested control is not effective, the combined risk of the assertions it supports moves to Not rely, and Procedure design suggests more tests of details. Record the deficiency as a finding. See also: Procedure design · Substantive procedures · Sampling · Journal entry testing · The Strategy and risks phase · The Planning phase
procedure-design: Set what you will test, control by control and account by account, before you test it. Who: the engagement team. Roles that only read (for example the quality reviewer) see the page in read-only mode. Procedure design (S5.5) Procedure design sets what you will test before you test it. It has two tabs: 1 Design of tests of controls: every control ticked To test on its class of transactions, with its Suggested size (from frequency and reliance) and your Planned size. A smaller planned size asks for a reason. 2 Design of tests of details: one block per significant account, with its combined risk. It is empty until accounts are significant and assessed. In tab 2, MSP means mandatory substantive procedure: it is ticked and locked for every relevant assertion. ASP means alternative substantive procedure: you tick the ones you choose. The tool highlights the alternatives suggested by the combined risk (red High, amber Moderate, green Low). Check the mandatory procedures of each account. Tick the alternatives you need. A High combined risk needs at least one alternative on that assertion before the account counts as designed. Click Add another procedure for a procedure of your own, and tick the assertions it answers. Click Draw the sample on a row that needs one: the sampling tool opens already filled with that account and its population. You can untick an alternative only until work on it starts. The library covers receivables, payables, inventory, fixed assets, cash, equity and borrowings; for other accounts you add your own procedures. See also: The combined risk assessment · Sampling · Substantive procedures
substantive: Perform the procedures designed, account by account, and record their results and findings. Who: the engagement team. Roles that only read (for example the quality reviewer) see the page in read-only mode. Working account by account The Substantive procedures page shows one card per significant account: green all done, amber in progress, grey not started, with the number of findings. Only procedures chosen in Procedure design appear. Click an account. It opens with one tab per procedure, in working order (mandatory first, then alternatives, then your own). Work through the Steps of the tab and record what you did. For a problem, click Raise a finding: describe The issue and, if needed, the Adjustment to book. An adjustment goes to the summary of audit differences by itself when you save. Choose the result (No exception or Exceptions found) and click Mark as done. Click Reopen to change it later. Procedures prepared from your uploads Some procedures are prepared by the tool from your uploads: the sub-ledger compared with the general ledger, the entries around year end for cut-off, the payments and invoices after year end (search for unrecorded liabilities), customer and supplier confirmations, the fixed asset register against the ledger (K-M1), the vouching of additions and disposals (K-M2) and the test counts and roll-forward of the inventory count (F-M1). When a file is missing, the tab says Data missing and offers Open the uploads. Lead schedules show the balances by index, with By account, with commentary, Open the general-ledger entries and Extract to Excel. One account, one tab per procedure, in working order. See also: Procedure design · Findings · The summary of audit differences · Analytics and the data tools
sampling: Draw a sample, record the audited values and conclude. Who: the engagement team. Roles that only read (for example the quality reviewer) see the page in read-only mode. Drawing a sample The Sampling page holds every sample of the engagement, with its reason, so each draw can be explained and repeated. Click Draw from a dataset (or Draw the sample from Procedure design, which fills it for you). Choose the Dataset and the method: Random, Systematic, Monetary unit (MUS) or Key items + random. Set the Sample size, and the Key-item threshold, Confidence and Expected misstatement where asked. To force a size, fill Size typed by hand and Why the size is typed by hand. Click Draw. Then enter the Audited value of every item. Click Record the conclusion, or Extend the sample if the projected error is above the tolerable misstatement. A projected error goes to the summary of audit differences (C1.1). See also: The Execution phase and tests of controls · Procedure design · Substantive procedures · The summary of audit differences
journal-entries: Select the journal entries that show signs of possible management override, test each one on the same screen, and conclude on journal entry testing (E3.1). Who: the engagement team. Roles that only read (for example the quality reviewer) see the page in read-only mode. One screen Open Engagement dashboard › Tools › Journal entry testing. Everything is on one screen, without tabs. This is the work ISA 240 asks for on journal entries. Four boxes at the top give the summary: Box What it shows General ledger in use Its lines, its entries and when it was loaded. Entries selected The entries found by at least one criterion. Tested How many of the selection are tested, without exceptions and with exceptions. Findings raised The findings, and the adjustments sent to the summary of audit differences. Criteria On the left, Criteria lists each criterion with a tick box and the number of entries it finds, in four groups: Group Criteria When it was posted Posted on a Sunday, Posted on a Saturday, Posted on a public holiday, Last 5 days of the year or first 5 days after (5 by default). Who posted it Same person prepared and approved, No approver recorded, Posted by a person who rarely posts entries. What it says Round amounts, Just below an approval limit, Missing or vague description, Rarely used or suspense accounts. Unusual account pairings Revenue against cash, Expenses paid in cash above a limit, Fixed assets against revenue, Payables against receivables, Revenue debited after year end, Equity against income or expense. The selection is every entry found by at least one criterion. Tick criteria to show only the entries they find; with nothing ticked, the table shows the whole selection. Clear the criteria removes the ticks. Under the criteria, one line gives the settings, set once for the engagement: the round amount (1 000 000), the approval limit (5 000 000, with a band of 10 %), the cash expense limit (500 000), the days around the year end (5), the rare poster (below 2 % of the entries), the rare account (fewer than 3 entries), the public holidays of the year (Cameroon calendar) and the vague words. Click Change the settings to adjust them. The selected entries On the right, the table shows each selected entry: Entry, Date (with the weekday), Journal, Accounts (debit → credit), Amount, Prepared / approved, Why selected and Test (To test, No exception or Exception).
