Click Export the selection for the client (Excel) to send the list to the client. Click an entry: its test opens below it. Answer the four questions, each Yes, No or Not applicable: Supporting document obtained and agreed to the entry (amount, date, accounts); Entry approved by an appropriate person, other than its preparer; Business reason understood and consistent with our knowledge of the entity; Recorded in the right accounts, period and amount. Write what you did in Work done and result. Cite the attachments as [A1], [A2]. If something is wrong, click Raise a finding (the finding goes to the Findings tool, linked to the entry and to E3.1) or Add an adjustment (it goes to the summary of audit differences and waits for the reviewer). The entry's conclusion follows the answers: Exception as soon as one answer is No; No exception when all four are answered and none is No. Journal entry testing: tick criteria, then test each selected entry. Findings, adjustments and sign-off At the bottom, Findings from journal entry testing lists the findings raised (Finding, Entry, Kind, Stage), and Adjustments to the summary of audit differences lists the adjustments (Entry, Heading, Adjustment proposed, Amount, Status). Under Conclusion and sign-off, click Sign as preparer; the reviewer then clicks Sign as reviewer. This signs working paper E3.1, with the usual sign-off rules. Entries reviewed before this screen keep their review: Cleared reads as No exception, Problem as Exception, and the note as Work done and result. See also: Analytics and the data tools · Findings · The Execution phase and tests of controls
data-tools: Record substantive analytical procedures, and use the analysers that do part of the work from the client's files. Who: the engagement team. Roles that only read (for example the quality reviewer) see the pages in read-only mode. Substantive analytics Substantive analytics records an analytical procedure as evidence: lead index, assertion, expectation, actual figure, threshold (a share of performance materiality, set by risk), difference and conclusion. Click Save a procedure to add one. The analysers The Data analytics tile opens the analysers. Each one lists the uploads of its kind, with Import a dataset and Download the template: Analyser What it holds Trial balance analyzer Upload, check and map the trial balance. General ledger analyzer The journal-entry population, its checks and The thirty analytics. Accounts receivable analyzer / Accounts payable analyzer Open items and ageing, Reconcile to the control account, Export the aging. Supplier statements Statements against the payables ledger. Bank analyzer Bank statements and outstanding items. Inventory analyzer The inventory listing, used for the test counts. Fixed assets analyzer The register, used by K-M1 and K-M2. Payroll analyzer The payroll register and its agreement to the balance. See also: Uploading the client's data · Substantive procedures · Journal entry testing
working-paper: Every standard working paper in AuditISA is laid out the same way: once you know one, you know them all. Who: everyone on the engagement team. The quality reviewer can read and raise notes but does not change the work. Opening the working paper This page walks through one example, S4.2 Going Concern, Preliminary (ISA 570). Click Strategy and risks in the top bar, then click S4.2 in the task list. You can also find it under Tasks. The working paper opens on one scrolling page in three columns: the step list on the left, the work in the middle, and the tools, attachments and assignment on the right. The layout of a working paper (here C2.2) The header Title and depth label: the code and name, then a label such as Non-complex · document by exception. Under it you see the client, the year, the standard, the edition (Edition: ISA in force) and the deadline. The deadline turns red when it has passed. Progress: for example "0 of 7 tasks done · not signed". It also counts tasks done in a tool, tasks closed by exception, and open review notes. Prepare / Review: two ways to read the same working paper. Prepare shows the tips and the full requirements. Review hides them so the reviewer sees only the work. See Review notes. Save the paper: nothing is recorded until you click it. The label beside it reads Unsaved changes, then Saved at and the time. If you try to leave with unsaved changes, AuditISA asks you to Stay or Leave without saving. The step list The left column lists 1 Objective, each task under 2 Tasks required (2.1 Financial indicators, 2.2 Operating indicators and so on), and 3 Conclusion and sign-off. Click a line to jump to it. A coloured dot shows each task's state, and a red dot with a number shows open review notes. Under Show only:, click Not done or Open notes to filter the list. 1 Objective This states in a few lines what the working paper must achieve. The standard link (for S4.2, ISA 570 (Revised 2024) ↗) opens the official text in a new tab. Click Full requirements to unfold what the standards ask in more detail, including the OHADA rule on equity below half of the share capital. 2 Tasks required On S4.2 a card called Pre-filled from the data comes first. It shows figures that AuditISA has read from the trial balance, here the equity, half of the share capital and the result of comparing them. Click Open the Financial analysis to see the detail. Each task then shows its text, its standard reference on the right (for example ISA 570 A3), and a Tip box you can fold away. To complete a task: Do the work described. Click Done and describe in the box what you did and found, with the working-paper reference. If the task does not apply, click Not applicable. A shaded box opens: the reason is required. Click Save the paper. A finished task folds to one line. Click it to open it again. A task marked Done in the tool was completed in a linked tool and needs nothing more on the working paper. How much you write depends on the profile The engagement profile, which comes from the profile questionnaire, sets how much documentation each working paper asks for. Profile What the tasks look like Complex · full documentation One text box per task. You describe the work and the result in full. Non-complex · document by exception Three buttons per task: No exceptions noted, Exceptions noted and Not applicable. With No exceptions noted, a standard answer is filled in for you and you must give a Source: a tool, a linked task or an attachment such as A1. With Exceptions noted, a box opens to describe the exceptions, their effect and what was done. Very simple · tick list and summary One tick box (or n/a) per task, then a single box, Summary of work performed: what was done, with whom, the documents seen and the result. The very simple layout When the working paper switches back to full documentation A lighter layout is never applied where it would be unsafe. The working paper opens in full documentation, whatever the profile, when: a tool has raised a warning on this working paper (for example, equity is below half of the share capital); a conclusion statement is answered No; the working paper is one that is never lightened (C1.1, C3.1, C5.5, C5.6 and C5.11). A line under the objective tells you why. If a task was closed as No exceptions noted before the warning appeared, AuditISA asks you to write the result instead. Findings and adjustments On S4.2, record a matter for the engagement file with the Findings tool in the right-hand column. Every finding raised from any working paper builds up in that one tool. On the working papers of substantive procedures (in Execution), each finding also appears at the bottom of the working paper in two parts: 1. Finding (the issue, and how and where it happened) and 2. Adjustment to book. When you save the adjustment it goes straight to the summary of audit differences. See Findings. The right-hand column Tools: links to the tools this working paper uses. For S4.2 these are Financial analysis, Significant accounts and Findings. Linked tasks: related working papers (S4.1, E6.3, C2.2 and others). Click one to open it. Its Back link brings you back here. Assignment: the Preparer, the Reviewer and the Deadline. A change applies at once and can be reversed with Undo. With no date of its own, the task takes its phase's deadline. Task not applicable: give a reason, then click Mark not applicable. Reinstate the task reverses it. A senior or above can do this; the quality reviewer cannot. Attachments: click Attach a file, or Pick from this engagement to reuse a document already in the engagement file. Each file gets a reference (A1, A2…). Cite it in your text as [A2] or as a Source. Uploading a file with the same name creates a new version. A removed file can be restored for 30 days. Attaching or removing a file after signing voids the signatures, because the evidence has changed. Review notes inside a task Under each task, + Review note on this task opens a small box. Type the point and click Add the note. The note stays inside the task, next to the work it concerns. See Review notes. 3 Conclusion and sign-off Answer each statement Yes or No. A No needs an explanation. Some statements are checked by a tool. If the tool disagrees with your answer, it shows the tool shows otherwise. On S4.2, fill in Work required at completion (E6.3) where needed. Write the Conclusion, or click Use the standard wording and adapt it. Click Save the paper, then Sign as preparer. If something is missing, Still to complete: lists it. Concluding the working paper If a colleague changes the same box while you are typing, your text is kept and theirs is shown underneath. You can choose Use their version, or save to replace it. See also: Review notes · Signing a working paper · Findings · The engagement questionnaire
review-notes: Review a working paper, then raise, answer and clear review notes on it. Who: any team member who can write may raise a note, and so can the quality reviewer. Anyone on the team can reply. Reviewing in Review mode Open the working paper and click Review in the header. The tips and full requirements are hidden, so you see only the work. Finished tasks fold to one line; click a line to open it. If tasks were closed with No exceptions noted, a blue banner tells you how many: check that each one has a convincing Source. Under Show only:, use Not done to find gaps and Open notes to follow up your points. Raising a review note Under the task concerned, click + Review note on this task. For a point on the conclusion, click + Review note on the conclusion in section 3. Type the point in Raise a review point. Click Add the note. The note shows your name and the date. The open notes are counted in the working paper's header and shown as a red dot in the step list. The Review notes list of the engagement Replying and clearing Reply: anyone on the team can type in Your reply and click Reply. The author of the note is told. A reply does not close the note: the reviewer decides whether the point is resolved. Clear: closes the note, which then reads Cleared. Only these people may clear a note: its author, or a manager or above who did not prepare the working paper. Notes are never deleted. Cleared notes stay on the working paper as part of the audit trail. A working paper with open review notes cannot be signed by the reviewer. Clear the notes first. See also: Signing a working paper, Working on a working paper
signing: Sign a working paper as preparer, reviewer, partner or quality reviewer, and see why a signature can be voided. Who: everyone on the team. Each person can sign only in the roles allowed, depending on your firm's sign-off policy. Signing a working paper The sign-off row at the bottom of section 3 shows one button or chip per role: Role Button Who Preparer Sign as preparer The person who did the work, at or above the minimum role of the sign-off policy. Reviewer Sign as reviewer A senior or above (or the policy's minimum), who is not the preparer. Partner Sign as partner A partner, where the task requires partner approval. Quality reviewer Sign as quality reviewer The engagement quality reviewer appointed on the team, where a quality review applies. Click Save the paper first. Check the line Still to complete:. Anything listed there blocks signing. Click your button. It becomes a chip with the role letter (P preparer, R reviewer, A partner approval, Q quality reviewer), your name and the date. Under the buttons, a line repeats this task's rule, for example "Preparer: Audit staff minimum · Reviewer: Senior minimum · Partner: required". It also tells you your role on the engagement and the roles you may sign in. The preparer always signs first. On a very simple engagement the preparer signs, then the partner. Some working papers also have a Section conclusion box. Where it appears, a senior or manager clicks Reviewed (senior/manager) before signing the working paper as reviewer. A signed working paper: the header shows who has signed No self-review If you signed a working paper as preparer, AuditISA will not let you review it. Another team member must do that. The firm's sign-off policy can also stop the same person being both preparer and reviewer in the task assignment. Why a signature is voided A signature covers the working paper exactly as it stood when it was signed. AuditISA keeps a fingerprint of the answers and the attached files at that moment. If someone changes an answer, attaches a file or removes one afterwards, the fingerprint no longer matches. The review signatures are then voided automatically with the reason "Paper content changed after sign-off". Voided signatures are listed under Voided signatures, with who signed, when and why the signature was voided. If no valid reviewer or partner signature is left, the working paper goes back to draft and must be signed again. The flag the wording has changed since means the standard text of the working paper was updated after you signed. Your signature stays valid, but it is worth a look. The flag signed by non-assignee means someone other than the assigned person signed. Removing your own sign-off Click your own chip (its hint reads Your sign-off: click to remove it). Confirm with Remove my sign-off, or click Cancel. Only the person who signed can remove that sign-off. If someone signed after you, their sign-off must be removed first. The working paper's status follows the signatures that remain. Every removal is recorded in the activity trail. The quality reviewer The engagement quality reviewer reads every working paper and raises review notes, but does not change the team's work. They record their own review on C4.2 Engagement Quality Review, which only the appointed quality reviewer completes and signs. See also: Review notes, Working on a working paper, Completing the audit
findings: The Findings tool holds every finding of the engagement, from the moment it is raised until it is closed. Who: preparers raise findings and write adjustments. The quality reviewer reads but does not change them. One register for the whole engagement Every finding, whatever working paper it was raised on, builds up in one place: the Findings tool. Open it from the Tools box of a working paper that lists it (S4.2, C1.1, C2.2 or C5.1, for example). A finding is one of three kinds: Kind Used for Matter for attention A point the partner or the next year should know about. Control deficiency A weakness in internal control, assessed under ISA 265 (likelihood and magnitude). Misstatement An error in the figures. It carries an adjustment and goes to the summary of audit differences. Raising a finding From the Findings tool: click New finding, choose the kind, give it a title and, if you like, the working paper it belongs to. From a working paper: on a substantive procedure, a line with an exception or a difference shows Raise a finding. The finding is linked to that working paper and appears under Findings on this working paper. In the Findings tool, click a row to open it on the right. Red marks a significant deficiency, amber a deficiency, and grey another matter or a misstatement. Open its working paper takes you back to where the finding was raised. The Findings tool Following a finding to its close A finding moves forward on its own as you fill it in. The filters across the top count the findings at each stage: Stage What you record 1 Raised What we found, Why it matters, What we recommend. 2 Assessed (ISA 265) For a control deficiency: Likelihood, Magnitude and the Severity that follows. 3 Discussed with management Management's answer. 4 Reported Reported in writing to (for example, the finance director) and the date of the letter. 5 Closed Under Close the finding, write how it was resolved, then Mark as closed. A closed finding can be opened again with Reopen the finding and a reason. Export to Excel gives you the whole register, for a management letter for example. The adjustment of a misstatement A misstatement finding has a section called Adjustment to book. Each line uses one of seven headings of the financial statements, not a trial balance account: Statement of financial position Income statement Non-current assets, Current assets, Non-current liabilities, Current liabilities, Equity Revenue, Expenditure For each line, pick the Heading, write a Label and enter the Debit or Credit. Use + Add a line for more. Choose the Nature: Factual, Judgemental or Projected. When the debits equal the credits, the editor shows Balanced ✓. Click Save. Saving sends the adjustment to the summary of audit differences by itself. Equity includes the effect on profit. Open the summary takes you there. See also: The summary of audit differences, Working on a working paper
audit-differences: The summary of audit differences gathers every adjustment of the engagement, to be reviewed, posted and sent to the client. Who: a reviewer posts the adjustments, depending on your firm's sign-off policy. The quality reviewer reads but does not change them. The summary of audit differences Open it from Summary of audit differences in the Tools box of C1.1. The differences come from the working papers. To add or change one, open its working paper. Click a line to see where it came from. The tabs are 1 Uncorrected, 2 Corrected, 3 Disclosures, 4 Cash flow, 5 Other factors and 6 Tax and conclusion. Brackets mean that the line reduces profit or the balance. Differences below the clearly trivial level are kept aside under Clearly trivial. They are not added to the total, and they are not lost (ISA 450). The Total uncorrected (before tax) and the materiality bar count every adjustment, posted or not. In 6 Tax and conclusion, enter the Tax rate (%) and write the Team conclusion: are the uncorrected differences material, alone or together? The summary of audit differences Reviewing and posting a line Use the Adjustments to review filter to see the lines not posted yet. If something is wrong, click Review note, write what the preparer should look at, and click Send. The line cannot be posted until the note is cleared with Clear the note. When you agree with the line, click Post. The person who prepared an adjustment cannot post it. Nor can the quality reviewer. Your firm's sign-off policy for C1.1 decides who may post. To change a posted line, click Unpost first. This is logged, and the line shows changed since posted until it is posted again. A posted line can still be marked as corrected by management. The client copy Only posted lines make up the client's list. Click Download the client copy (posted only) to get the Excel file that you send to management with your request to correct. The Posted (client copy) column shows which lines it holds. The C1.1 working paper C1.1 Summary of Audit Differences is where you conclude. A card at the top shows the totals from the summary. Its tasks follow ISA 450: accumulate, classify, communicate, obtain the reasons for not correcting, reassess materiality and evaluate individually and in aggregate. C1.1 is never lightened, whatever the profile. See also: Findings, Completing the audit
completing: The Conclusion phase holds the final reviews, the representation letter, the reports and the engagement partner's approval. Who: the whole team. The quality reviewer completes C4.2. The engagement partner approves on C4.1. The Conclusion phase at a glance Click Conclusion in the top bar. The tasks are grouped as follows: Group Tasks Summary of audit differences C1.1 Summary of Audit Differences, C1.2 Summary Review Memorandum, C1.3 Consultation Record Final review of the financial statements C2.1 Final Overall Review (ISA 520), C2.2 Subsequent Events and Going Concern Representations C3.1 Representation Letters (ISA 580) Review and approval C4.1 Review and Approval, C4.2 Engagement Quality Review, C4.3 Points Outstanding Statutory reports C5.1 Opinion and report (ISA 700–706), C5.3 Regulated Agreements, C5.4 Article 715 Board Report, C5.10 Article 525 Attestation Communications and legal procedures C5.11 Communications (ISA 260/265), C5.2 Statutory Deadlines Calendar, C5.5 to C5.9 (alert procedure, criminal offences, securities register, equity against half of the capital, joint auditor) Documentation and archiving C6.1 Archive Checklist, C6.2 Documentation and Archive Which tasks you see depends on the client's legal form and on the engagement profile. For example, C5.7 does not apply to an SARL. Every working paper works as described in Working on a working paper. Subsequent events and going concern (C2.2) C2.2 brings your going concern work to its final conclusion. It starts from the preliminary view in S4.2 and the execution work in E6.3. Carry your procedures up to the report date, make a final inquiry of management, read the minutes since your last reading, and decide whether each event requires an adjustment or a disclosure. Then conclude whether the going concern basis is appropriate and whether a material uncertainty exists. The card at the top repeats the equity figures from the trial balance. The representation letter (C3.1) Open Templates in the Tools box to start from the firm's letter. Add the representations specific to this engagement and the materiality used in the letter. Have the partner review the draft before it goes to the client. Attach the signed letter. It must be dated no later than the auditor's report. C3.1 is always in full documentation, whatever the profile. Reports and communications C5.1 Opinion and report records the opinion, the components of the report, going concern, key audit matters, any emphasis or other matter, and the report date. Its tools are Summary of audit differences, Materiality and Findings. The other statutory reports (C5.3, C5.4, C5.10) cover the OHADA special reports. C5.11 records what you told those charged with governance and management, including the control deficiencies from the Findings tool. Quality review (C4.2) Where an engagement quality review is required, the quality reviewer evaluates the team's significant judgements. They raise review notes on the working papers and record their review on C4.2. Only the appointed quality reviewer completes and signs C4.2. The review must be complete before the report is dated. Partner review and approval (C4.1, C4.3) On C4.3 Points Outstanding, list what is still open and clear each point with evidence. On C4.1 Review and Approval, the engagement partner confirms that every planned procedure was performed and every working paper is signed. Every point outstanding must be cleared and no review note left open. The misstatements must be evaluated, the quality review complete, and the evidence must support the opinion. Its Tools box links to Review notes, Audit programs and Team. Work after the report date After the report date, only assembly work is allowed. A new finding, misstatement or procedure conclusion is refused unless a manager or above clicks Open, with this reason under Work after the report date and gives the reason. Each item recorded is then named in the activity trail. Close the work after the report date ends it. See also: The completion checklist and issuing the report, The summary of audit differences, Archiving the engagement file
completion-checklist: The completion checklist shows whether the engagement is ready, and is where the engagement partner signs off and issues the report. Who: the team answers the questions. Only the engagement partner signs the checklist and issues the report. The completion checklist Open C6.1 and click Completion checklist. The page has two parts: 1 · Checked by the tool: checks that AuditISA runs on the engagement by itself: every task addressed, every working paper signed and reviewed, every review note cleared, controls and substantive procedures concluded, and significant deficiencies communicated. Each check is green or red, and a red one names the tasks concerned. 2 · Confirmed by the team — a note is required for each answer: thirteen questions, for example "Subsequent events reviewed up to the report date" and "Independence re-confirmed by every team member". Answer Yes or No and write a note. Only a Yes with its note turns green. The completion checklist Issuing the report When every line is green, the engagement partner clicks Partner sign-off: ready to issue. The partner then clicks Issue the report, which appears on the same page once the partner has signed, and confirms. The report date is recorded. If an answer changes after the partner has signed, the sign-off is voided. The partner signs again before the report is issued. See also: Completing the audit, Archiving the engagement file
archiving: Assemble and archive the engagement file once the report is issued, and add to it later by addendum only. Who: any accepted team member who can write may archive (not the quality reviewer). Legal holds need a manager or above. The assembly period After the report date you have sixty days to assemble the final engagement file (ISA 230). Open C6.2 and click Assemble and archive. The page shows how many days are left. The counter turns amber when fewer than fifteen days remain. During this time, do only assembly work: tidy the working papers, file the signed documents and clear what is left. See Completing the audit for work after the report date. Archiving the engagement file On the Assemble and archive page, check the column on the left. Every line must be green. Under Before archiving, answer the two confirmations with Yes and a note: the signed report, financial statements and representation letter are filed, and the permanent file is updated. Read What archiving does. Type the client's name in the box to confirm, then click Archive the file. If the sixty days have passed, AuditISA asks for the reason for the late archive. The reason is kept in the trail. Archiving cannot be undone. An archived engagement file can be opened again for reading only. Assembling and archiving What archiving does The whole engagement file becomes read-only: nothing can be edited or deleted. Each page shows Read only: this engagement is archived. A sealed copy is made. It holds every working paper (as PDF where possible, otherwise as a web page), all the evidence, and a fingerprint (SHA-256) of each file. The fingerprint proves later that nothing has changed. The sealed copy is kept on the server and in the backups. A team member can click Download the sealed copy. Each download is logged. The team and inspectors can still open and read the engagement file. Every opening is listed in the Access log. Adding something after archiving: addenda Sometimes something must be added after the engagement file is closed, such as a late document or an answer to an inspector. You do not change the archive: you add an addendum (ISA 230 ¶16). On the archive page, under Addenda after archiving (ISA 230 ¶16), click Add an addendum. Write why: what is added, and who asked for it. Attach the document if there is one. Click Add the addendum. An addendum adds to the engagement file. It never changes or removes what was archived. The list shows who added it, when and why. Retention and legal hold An archived engagement file is kept for at least ten years from the report date, as OHADA practice requires. It cannot be deleted before that date. If a dispute or an inquiry is expected, a manager or above can click Place a legal hold and give a reason. While the hold is on, the engagement file cannot be deleted, even after its retention period. Release the legal hold lifts it. See also: The completion checklist and issuing the report, Rolling forward to next year
roll-forward: Start next year's engagement from a closed one, carrying its setup, answers and evidence as drafts. Who: a manager or above on the team. Rolling forward to next year You can start next year's engagement from a closed one, meaning its report is issued or its engagement file is archived. Open the engagement record of last year's engagement and click Roll forward. Under 1 · What to carry, untick anything you do not want to carry. Everything is ticked by default. Under 2 · Year, team and process, check the Year end and the Engagement partner. Choose the Approach: Same as last year keeps last year's tasks, and Change reopens the profile questionnaire. Review the Team. Last year's members are listed. Tick or untick Invite, change a Role, or add a line with an email and role for a new member. People who have left the firm are not carried. Click Create the file. Carried (as drafts to update or re-confirm) How it arrives Tasks and scope (profile answers) The questionnaire must be concluded again. Materiality basis and percentages No amounts: they are worked out from this year's figures. Classes of transactions, controls and walkthrough notes Every test result, conclusion and sign-off starts again. Risk register, procedure design, significance decisions As drafts, each one to re-confirm. Procedures are not started. Prior-year balances Last year's closing trial balance becomes the comparatives (ISA 510). Working paper answers Marked "Carried forward from (year): to update". All of last year's evidence Copied and marked "Prior year, carried forward: review before relying on it". Click Mark as reviewed once you have checked a file. Sign-offs, conclusions and independence always start again in the new engagement. Review notes, completion records, the done or not-applicable ticks of procedures, and the answers of C4.1, C4.2, C6.1 and C6.2 are not carried either. See also: Archiving the engagement file, Completing the audit
faq: Short answers to the questions auditors ask most often. Who: everyone. My review signature has disappeared. Why? Someone changed the working paper after you signed: an answer, or a file attached or removed. Your signature covered the earlier version, so it was voided. You will find it under Voided signatures with the date and reason. Review the change and sign again. See Signing a working paper. Why can't I sign as reviewer? The most common reasons: you signed the same working paper as preparer (no self-review), review notes are still open, the preparer has not signed yet, or your role is below the minimum in your firm's sign-off policy. The message on screen tells you which one applies. I clicked "No exceptions noted" but it is greyed out. A tool has raised a warning on this working paper, so it must be documented in full. Describe the work and the result in the text box instead. Why does my working paper show a text box per task when the client is non-complex? The working paper went back to full documentation because a tool raised a warning, a conclusion statement is answered No, or the working paper is one that is never lightened. A line under the objective tells you which. I lost my changes. Nothing is recorded until you click Save the paper. Watch for Unsaved changes next to the button. If you try to leave a working paper with unsaved changes, AuditISA asks you first. Two of us edited the same working paper at the same time. Each person's changes are kept where they do not overlap. If you both changed the same box, your text stays and your colleague's version is shown underneath with Use their version. Who can clear my review note? Only these people may clear a note: you, as its author, or a manager or above who did not prepare the working paper. Anyone on the team can reply. See Review notes. How do I correct an adjustment that is already posted? A reviewer clicks Unpost on the summary of audit differences. Change the adjustment on its working paper, then have it posted again. The unposting is logged. Can I unarchive an engagement file? No. An archived engagement file stays sealed and read-only. To add something, use Add an addendum on the archive page. See Archiving the engagement file. The Roll forward button refuses to start. An engagement can be rolled forward only once it is closed: its report issued or its engagement file archived. You also need to be a manager or above on the team. A file in the new year is marked "Prior year, carried forward". It was copied from last year. Check that it still holds, then click Mark as reviewed. See Rolling forward to next year.
words: The words AuditISA uses on its screens, and what they mean. Who: everyone. Word Meaning Engagement One audit: one client, one financial year, with its own engagement file and team. Profile The result of the profile questionnaire: Complex, Non-complex or Very simple. It sets which tasks the engagement file holds and how much each working paper asks you to write. Task / working paper One item of the file index (for example S4.2). Its working paper holds the objective, the tasks required, the conclusion and the signatures. Document by exception On non-complex engagements, one click (No exceptions noted) plus a source when nothing is wrong. You write text only when exceptions are noted. Source Where the evidence for an answer is: a tool, a linked task or an attachment reference. Attachment reference (A1, A2…) The number each file gets on a working paper. Cite it as [A2]. Review note A question or point raised on a task or a conclusion. It stays open until cleared, and is never deleted. Sign-off policy / matrix The firm's rules on the minimum role that may prepare, review and approve each task. Set under Firm settings. Voided signature A signature cancelled automatically because the working paper changed after signing. Quality reviewer The engagement quality reviewer (ISQM 2). They review independently, raise notes and complete C4.2, but do not change the team's work. Finding A matter for attention, a control deficiency or a misstatement, recorded in the Findings tool. Adjustment The debit and credit lines that would correct a misstatement, using the seven headings of the financial statements. Summary of audit differences The list of all adjustments (C1.1), compared with materiality (ISA 450). Post / posted A reviewer's acceptance of an adjustment line. Only posted lines go to the client copy. Clearly trivial A difference below the trivial threshold. It is kept aside, not added to the total. Lead schedule The summary of an area's accounts from the trial balance, against the prior year, which the working papers start from. MSP Mandatory substantive procedure: it must be performed for the assertion. ASP Alternative substantive procedure: chosen when the procedures are designed, to respond to the risk. Completion checklist The tool checks and thirteen team questions on C6.1. The partner signs it before the report is issued. Report date The date the auditor's report is issued. After it, only assembly work is allowed. Assembly period The sixty days after the report date for completing the final engagement file. Archive / sealed copy The locked, read-only engagement file, with a copy whose every file carries a fingerprint (SHA-256). Addendum Something added to an archived engagement file, with who, when and why. The original stays untouched. Legal hold A block on deleting an engagement file, for disputes or inquiries, even after its retention period. Roll-forward Creating next year's engagement from a closed one, carrying setup, answers and evidence as drafts. Carried forward A mark on an answer or file that came from last year and still needs updating or reviewing. See also: English-French glossary, Working on a working paper, Review notes, Findings
